# Data visualization {#sec-visualization} Julia has three reasonable routes to graphics, all resting on [**Makie.jl**](https://docs.makie.org) [@danisch2021makie]: | Route | For whom | |---|---| | `TidierPlots.jl` | people coming from `ggplot2` who want the same grammar | | `AlgebraOfGraphics.jl` | people who want an idiomatically Julian grammar of graphics | | Plain `Makie.jl` | full control over the figure | This chapter shows all three on the same data, because the right choice depends on the task — and because knowing how to translate between them keeps you from getting stuck. ::: {#cell-setup-06 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using TidierData using CairoMakie using AlgebraOfGraphics using CSV, DataFrames CairoMakie.activate!(type = "png") ponds = CSV.read(joinpath("..", "data", "ponds.csv"), DataFrame) ponds_c = @chain ponds begin @drop_missing(canopy) @mutate(log_area = log(area_m2)) end nrow(ponds_c) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#fig-tidierplots-scatter .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` Richness against canopy cover, by region. ::: ::: ::: {.r-equivalent} **In R** ```r ggplot(ponds_c, aes(x = canopy, y = richness, colour = region)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.7) + labs(x = "Canopy cover (%)", y = "Species richness") ``` The translation is nearly character for character; the difference is the `@` in `@aes`. ::: ## `AlgebraOfGraphics.jl`: an algebraic grammar {#sec-aog} AoG treats plots as an algebra: `*` combines layers, `+` superimposes them. ::: {#cell-fig-aog-scatter .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} plt = AlgebraOfGraphics.data(ponds_c) * mapping(:canopy => "Canopy cover (%)", :richness => "Species richness", color = :region => "Region") * (visual(Scatter, alpha = 0.6) + AlgebraOfGraphics.linear()) draw(plt; figure = (size = (700, 450),)) ``` ::: {#fig-aog-scatter .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` The same plot in AlgebraOfGraphics, with a linear fit per region. ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note} `AlgebraOfGraphics.data` and `AlgebraOfGraphics.linear` are qualified because the names `data` and `linear` collide with other loaded packages. In a script using only AoG, `data(...)` and `linear()` suffice. ::: ## Facets {#sec-facets} ::: {#cell-fig-facets .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} plt = AlgebraOfGraphics.data(ponds_c) * mapping(:log_area => "log(area)", :richness => "Richness", color = :region, layout = :hydro) * (visual(Scatter, alpha = 0.6) + AlgebraOfGraphics.linear()) draw(plt; figure = (size = (800, 400),)) ``` ::: {#fig-facets .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` Richness–area relationship faceted by hydroperiod. ::: ::: ## Distributions {#sec-distributions} ::: {#cell-fig-boxplot .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} plt = AlgebraOfGraphics.data(ponds_c) * mapping(:region => "Region", :richness => "Richness", color = :hydro => "Hydroperiod", dodge = :hydro) * visual(BoxPlot) draw(plt; figure = (size = (700, 420),)) ``` ::: {#fig-boxplot .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` Richness distribution by region and hydroperiod. ::: ::: ## Plain `Makie.jl`: full control {#sec-makie} When a figure needs a layout the grammar cannot express, drop down to Makie. ::: {#cell-fig-makie-composite .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} fig = Figure(size = (860, 380)) ax1 = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel = "Canopy cover (%)", ylabel = "Richness", title = "(a) Canopy") scatter!(ax1, ponds_c.canopy, ponds_c.richness, color = (:steelblue, 0.6)) ax2 = Axis(fig[1, 2], xlabel = "log(area)", ylabel = "Richness", title = "(b) Area") scatter!(ax2, ponds_c.log_area, ponds_c.richness, color = (:darkorange, 0.6)) ax3 = Axis(fig[1, 3], xlabel = "Richness", ylabel = "Frequency", title = "(c) Distribution") hist!(ax3, ponds_c.richness, bins = 12, color = (:seagreen, 0.7)) fig ``` ::: {#fig-makie-composite .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` A composite figure assembled by hand with Makie. ::: ::: Makie's layout system is grid-based (`fig[row, col]`), covering the role of `patchwork` and `cowplot` in R without an extra package. ## Saving figures {#sec-saving} ::: {#saving .cell execution_count=0} ``` {.julia .cell-code} save("figure.png", fig; px_per_unit = 3) # high-resolution raster save("figure.pdf", fig) # vector, for publication save("figure.svg", fig) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-tip} ## Choosing a backend `CairoMakie` produces publication-quality static output (PNG, PDF, SVG) and is what this book uses. `GLMakie` opens GPU-accelerated interactive windows — useful for exploring data, unsuitable for rendering a book. ::: ## Exercises {.unnumbered} 1. Redo @fig-tidierplots-scatter using `temp_c` on the x axis. Does the pattern hold? 2. Build a two-panel figure: richness by region on the left, focal-species occurrence proportion by region on the right. 3. Translate @fig-facets to `TidierPlots.jl` using `facet_wrap`.
